newsitem.title: USA: ITT could make counterbid for Hilton - paper.
newsitem.headline: ITT could make counterbid for Hilton - paper.

text.p: ITT Corp is expected to take radical steps following Hilton Hotels Corp's unsolicited $6.5 billion bid for ITT, including the possibility of a counterbid for Hilton, according to an article in Barron's.
Barron's said the counterbid strategy, often referred to as the Pac-Man defense, was made popular by Martin Marietta, which used it successfully to fend off hostile bidder Bendix.

The paper said ITT also could buy in shares. It speculated that ITT could refuse to deactivate its poison-pill plan as Hilton has requested, in which case rights would issued making a takeover prohibitively expensive if an unwanted suitor accumulated a 15 percent stake.

Barron's also said it is unlikely that ITT will remain in its present form. "It's gone, once the atomic bomb is thrown," said Mario Gabelli, noted media investor and one of ITT's and Hilton's biggest shareholders.

The "atomic bomb" was Hilton's formal tender Friday, which came an unusually long time after the offer was made, according to Barron's. Barron's also said ITT is not expected to grant Hilton CEO Stephen Bollenbach's request for an early meeting with ITT, as Bollenbach had requested January 31.
